newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BUSINESSES BULLISH ON ECONOMIES - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BUSINESSES BULLISH ON ECONOMIES - SURVEY.

text.p: Businesses around the world are bullish about their own country's economic prospects in the next year, according to a study released Wednesday by Research International.
The study, which polled senior executives from over 1,400 companies in 43 countries, found that 52 percent were confident about economic growth in their home market, up from 40 percent last year.
Executives from Britain and China were among the most positive, with 80 percent expecting their economies to improve in the next year.
Asia Pacific-based companies were downbeat, with only 45 percent optimistic about their own growth prospects, down steeply from 72 percent last year.

"The downturn in confidence experienced within these Asia Pacific countries is mirrored by how the rest of the world perceive them; only a quarter of companies world-wide now cite South East Asia as their top expansion priority, compared to 33 percent last year," the study said.
Research International is a market research company with offices in 57 countries.
